title: Power Automate: time and cost savings rules for desktop flows
summary: Hold: the briefing calls licensing unpublished, but Microsoft's product licensing page already includes the full set of desktop automation capabilities in Power Automate Premium. It should distinguish that published entitlement from an unpublished savings-specific requirement or charge. The roadmap facts and the documented savings controls are supported; the control paths and API formatting need minor corrections.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because Microsoft has not published a licence requirement for desktop flow savings.
claims.quote: With a Power Automate Premium user license, users gain the full set of capabilities for cloud and desktop automation including premium connectors, process and task mining, AI Builder, use of managed environments, and Microsoft Dataverse storage.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the unqualified unpublished-licensing statements in the notes, body, open question and cost rationale with: 'Power Automate Premium includes the full set of cloud and desktop automation capabilities. A savings-specific licence requirement, price or meter is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/power-automate-licensing/types in sources and beside this statement. Do not claim Premium is the only licensing route or that unattended execution is included in it.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The environment money-saving control is reached through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Manage. ... select Environments. ... select an environment. ... select Settings. ... Expand Product, and then select Features. ... Savings ... Disable money-saving rules.
claims.fix: Make the setting's location explicit in the structured and rendered path: 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Savings > Disable money-saving rules'. The cited page gives the printed navigation and places the setting under Savings; the omitted section is not a different navigation choice.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row and Organization explanation
claims.claim: PATCH of the v9.2 Organization row with ismoneysavingsallowed set to false disables makers' permission to create money-saving rules.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations ... Operations supported: GETPATCH ... ismoneysavingsallowed ... Edm.Boolean ... Indicates whether the maker can create Power Automate money based saving rules.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api.call and the rendered call to 'PATCH <organization-uri>/api/data/v9.2/organizations(<organization-id>)'. Replace the note's API sentence with 'The request body sets ismoneysavingsallowed to false to disable permission to create money-saving rules.' The documented property and value are correct; the standard requires the body and headers outside the call.

claims.claim: Agents' savings are not affected by the Flow Aggregation retention setting.

claims.claim: Viewing and editing agent-flow savings rules requires a security role with privileges to Saving Rule and Flow Aggregation.

claims.claim: Dataverse PATCH update requests can use Content-Type: application/json and If-Match: *.
claims.quote: Update operations use the HTTP PATCH verb. ... The If-Match: * header ensures you don't create a new record by accidentally performing an upsert operation. ... Content-Type: application/json
claims.fix: Remove ', Content-Type: application/json, If-Match: *' from both structured and rendered calls when reducing them to method and path. The headers are valid, but their supporting Basic update reference is not cited: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/update-delete-table-rows.
